name: Moroccan Sultanate
locator: Printed p. 799, Area and Population, regional estimate for 1889.
definition: Alternate contemporary estimate assembled from the former kingdoms of Fez and Morocco, Tafilalt and Sijilmasa, and Sous, Adrar and northern Draa. None of the four region counts are delimited as partitions of the WWO territorial polygon. This is an overlapping comparison to the later five-million estimates.

name: Moroccan Sultanate
locator: Printed p. 799, Area and Population, general estimate.
definition: Publication-year estimate for the Sultan's dominions with no enumeration date. The source calls the southern frontier unsettled and estimates area at 219,000 square miles. The tally has no separate lines for the southern frontier or Spanish municipalities. Its numerical match to the legacy account does not establish the legacy source or a common perimeter with the map.

name: Moroccan Sultanate
method: retrospective demographic estimate quoted by the statistical office
definition: Rounded 1900 estimate as reported by HCP. Escallier's original geography and calculation were not recovered. The opening map perimeter and the independent estimate built from later protectorate and Tangier series cannot be equated.

name: Ceuta
definition: Separate Spanish municipal census geography. The opening border layer has no dedicated Ceuta polygon in this area. Inclusion in the Moroccan five-million estimates is undocumented. The census figure does not support an arithmetic deduction from those estimates.

name: Melilla
definition: Separate Spanish municipal census geography. The point falls inside the simplified Moroccan polygon and has no dedicated Melilla polygon. Inclusion in the Moroccan five-million estimates is undocumented. The census figure does not support an arithmetic deduction from those estimates.
